conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello Mr. Johnson, I'm Dr. Patel. I'll be your doctor during this stay. You were admitted for diarrhea and vomiting. Can you tell me more about what’s been going on?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi, yes. I’ve had six watery bowel movements last night, and two episodes of yellow vomit. No blood in the toilet, but I saw some on the tissue. I feel weak and thirsty.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. Any abdominal pain, fever, or dizziness?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, no pain or fever. I’m not lightheaded. But I’ve lost about 30 pounds in the last six weeks. My appetite’s been poor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s significant. You mentioned your son’s family was sick recently?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, a few of them had vomiting starting four days ago. We spent time together last week.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That helps. Given your history, especially the recent adenovirus infection, we’re concerned about another gastrointestinal infection. We’ll run some tests.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Could it be adenovirus again? I was just treated for that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s possible. We’ve sent a PCR test for adenovirus, but results will take a few days. In the meantime, we’re treating you for dehydration with IV fluids.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. My kidneys have been bad before—could this affect them?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your creatinine was elevated at 4.0, which is higher than your baseline of around 2.0–2.5. This is likely due to dehydration from vomiting and diarrhea. We expect it to improve with fluids.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my heart? I’ve had fluid issues before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good question. Your chest X-ray shows stable heart size, no new fluid in the lungs. We’ve held your Lasix for now to avoid over-diuresis while you're dehydrated.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Makes sense. I’ve been on prednisone and CellCept for GVHD—CellCept was stopped recently.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’re continuing your low-dose prednisone, Bactrim, and valacyclovir. GVHD is less likely since you’re improving without steroid escalation.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve also had some neck pain and burning when I pee lately.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We checked your urine—it shows no infection. The neck pain isn’t associated with stiffness or light sensitivity, so we don’t suspect meningitis. We’ll keep an eye on it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your stool tests came back—no C. diff, no salmonella, shigella, or parasites. Norovirus is negative too.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So not C. diff again? That’s good, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, that’s good. It means we don’t need antibiotics. We still suspect a viral infection, possibly adenovirus. Your kidney function is already improving—creatinine down to 3.4.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. Can I eat anything yet?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re starting you on a low-residue, lactose-free diet. Small meals first—let’s see how you tolerate it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your creatinine is now 2.7, and potassium has normalized. You’re doing well. We’re going to restart Lasix at a lower dose—40 mg instead of 60 mg.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Why lower it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Because your weight is down to 214.9 pounds from 217.6, and we don’t want to over-diurese. We’re balancing heart and kidney function.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. Any update on the adenovirus test?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Still pending. But since your symptoms are resolving without specific antiviral treatment, it may not change management.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve had no diarrhea for two days, and labs continue to improve. We’re confident you’re on the mend.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. I feel stronger. Can I go home soon?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re planning for discharge tomorrow if all goes well. You’ll go home with services—someone to check in on you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I’ll need help with meals and meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: All set for discharge today. Your adenovirus PCR is still pending, but we’ll follow up with you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my Lasix? I’m on 40 mg now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, 40 mg daily. We’ll adjust if needed. Weigh yourself every morning—call if you gain more than three pounds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. What about the small bump on my arm where the IV was?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s a small fluid collection—likely from the IV. It’s mildly tender but not infected. It should resolve on its own.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. And my other meds—same as before?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, same doses: prednisone, Bactrim, valacyclovir, pantoprazole, metoprolol, and the others. Continue all as prescribed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been depressed lately—still on escitalopram?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, and we encourage you to follow up with your mental health provider. Don’t stop it suddenly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I won’t. Any restrictions?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Avoid heavy lifting. Use your walker as needed. Stay hydrated, but don’t overdo fluids. Watch for nausea, fever, or swelling.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And when do I see my oncologist?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your follow-up is scheduled in five days. They’ll review the adenovirus and HHV-6 results when they come back.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: HHV-6? Was that tested?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, sent during this admission. It was checked due to your immunocompromised state, but results are still pending.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. I’ll keep an eye on things and call if anything changes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. You’re doing well. We’re discharging you home with services. A nurse will call tomorrow to check in.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor. I appreciate all the care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and we’ll see you soon in follow-up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just a quick call to check in—how are you feeling at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Much better. No diarrhea, eating well, and I’ve been weighing myself daily.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Excellent. Keep it up. We’ll get your test results soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Final update: your adenovirus PCR and HHV-6 results are still pending, but given your recovery, they won’t change your care plan.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Understood. I’ll follow up with my team.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, they’ll have the results soon. Continue all medications and monitoring.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will do. Thanks again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care, Mr. Johnson.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just confirming your discharge is official as of today. You’ve completed your admission successfully.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. I’m home and doing well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. Stay in touch with your care team.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you for everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You're very welcome. Get some rest.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I plan to.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Have a good recovery.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks, Doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care.
